PullRequest.Title: Experiment with card-style stacked diffs in Agents changes view
PullRequest.Body: ## Problem Stacked multi-file diffs can be difficult to scan: file boundaries are not always obvious, and the hidden-lines control can be mistaken for the end of a file while scrolling. ## Solution Adds an experimental, default-off Card presentation for the Agents Changes view, built on the current stacked-diff architecture: - **Card boundaries:** inset, rounded file surfaces make transitions between files easier to identify. - **Collapsible file headers:** reduce noise while preserving active, focused, hover, and high-contrast states. - **Quieter hidden-lines control:** uses the Sessions list "See more" visual pattern so it reads as an in-file action rather than a file boundary. The row remains reserved when expanded to avoid layout jumps. - **Preserved navigation:** incremental reveal, dragging, scroll anchoring, and symbol breadcrumbs continue to work. - **Accessibility:** the full-row disclosure and individual breadcrumbs are separate keyboard-accessible actions; long breadcrumbs truncate cleanly. - **Feature gating:** existing behavior is unchanged unless `"sessions.changes.cardView": true` is enabled and the window is reloaded. - **Regression coverage:** adds focused interaction, routing, accessibility, and component-fixture coverage. This does not replace the finalized stacked-diff implementation; it adds a presentation variant for experimentation. ## Screenshots | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Before | After | | --- | --- | | Before | After | | --- | --- | ## Validation - Client transpilation - TypeScript and CSS linting - Focused `MultiDiffEditorWidget` and `SessionChangesService` tests: 11 passing - Pre-commit hygiene and `git diff --check`

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or restore the Agents Changes editor with sessions.changes.cardView enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The startup contribution reads the already-loaded configuration and registers the custom pane; opening then creates SessionChangesEditorInput, which lazily delegates to the same MultiDiffEditorInput and must resolve all file models before its view model is applied. Registration itself has no I/O and is not a new blocking boundary.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve original and modified text-model references for each changed file through ITextModelService
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to two model-reference resolutions per changed file, launched across N files; cache/provider behavior can make warm resolutions cheaper.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The plain multi-diff editor already constructed MultiDiffEditorInput and used this identical model-resolution path; the new SessionChangesEditorInput delegates to one inner MultiDiffEditorInput rather than duplicating it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All document promises complete before the multi-diff model is returned and the editor view model is applied.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number N of changed files in the active session; model resolution performs up to 2N original/modified resource references, while visible diff-editor DOM remains virtualized.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The unchanged MultiDiffEditorInput maps all resources to promises, resolves each original/modified pair with Promise.allSettled, and awaits all file promises with Promise.all. The wrapper introduced for card mode adds no additional model-resolution pass or limiter change.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: SessionChangesEditorInput creates and retains one lazy inner MultiDiffEditorInput per input. Repeated getViewModel calls reuse its LazyStatefulPromise; warm text models are reused through model references. The card setting is read once at startup as documented.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed service routes card mode through the custom input, and that input directly delegates to a single unchanged MultiDiffEditorInput.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual provider latency and warm-model hit rate vary by resource scheme and workspace, but the PR does not change their count or scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the extra wrapper/header UI is bounded per editor, while expensive per-file model resolution, concurrency, and caching are unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Scroll a card-style stacked multi-file diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Scroll layout renders only virtualized multi-diff items near the viewport. A bound item creates one DiffEditorWidget and its card CSS/unchanged-region widgets; offscreen unfocused bindings are released and templates are pooled with a cap of five unused templates.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Visible/buffered diff items rather than total changed-file count, plus the number of unchanged regions inside those bound files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Rendering and browser layout run synchronously on the UI thread; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network operation is added by card styling or class-name construction.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Virtualized templates are reused; offscreen bindings are cleared unless focused, and at most five unused templates remain pooled per template type. CSS and variant configuration are static.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: VirtualizedItemManager disposal/pooling and the changed DiffEditorItemTemplate wiring establish the lifecycle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Viewport buffer size and unchanged-region density vary, but ownership is explicitly bounded by virtualization and pooling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the diff adds static classes, borders, and bounded DOM to already-rendered items without defeating virtualization or adding a layout read-after-write loop.

Scenarios.Scenario: Expand, collapse, or drag hidden unchanged-line regions in card mode
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The interaction updates UnchangedRegion observables, hidden areas, view-zone positions, labels, and scroll anchoring synchronously. Card mode intentionally retains the 40px control so collapse remains available and layout does not jump.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: R unchanged regions in currently bound diff editors; each region has paired original/modified view zones, with only the visible side exposing the interactive card content.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Observable reactions and editor layout are serialized on the UI thread. No external boundary is reached.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Card mode short-circuits shouldHideControls in the view-zone collection, so toggling does not tear down and reconstruct all overlay widgets. Existing widgets update their labels/icons; fully revealed regions skip breadcrumb lookup. Disposal follows the bound DiffEditorWidget lifecycle.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed lines keep controls present, while surrounding derived ownership and virtualization bound them and eliminate rebuilds on each toggle.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Files with exceptionally many separated hunks increase retained per-region DOM and layout rows, but that row is required by the new collapse UX and avoids reconstruction; no evidence establishes harmful magnitude under realistic viewport-bound use.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: retained per-region controls are an intentional bounded scheduling/layout tradeoff and avoid repeated widget reconstruction; there is no high-confidence performance bug.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup with card mode disabled (default)
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The BlockStartup contribution is instantiated as before, reads one boolean setting, and immediately returns without registering the custom editor when neither single-pane nor card mode is enabled.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant per-window startup work, independent of sessions or changed files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous configuration lookup only; no new asynchronous work or external boundary.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration is already available through IConfigurationService and read once; no cache or retained collection is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed constructor condition and default-false registration are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact lookup duration is unmeasured but constant and trivial compared with startup registration.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: default startup adds only a constant in-memory configuration read and preserves the early return.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 16 changed files and all diff pages. Traced startup/editor routing, per-file model resolution, multi-diff virtualization, card rendering, and unchanged-region interaction/lifecycle. No diff-introduced high-confidence performance regression was found.
